Content:
Area measures how much space there is on a flat surface. In this lesson, we'll learn about the various measurement units of area and how they relate to units of length.

Content:
Consider a square with sides of length [MATH: 1\,\textrm{m},] shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/9d0c9dfd6d8fd78ebbb6732f2d862b2b]

Content:
To find the area of a square, we multiply its side lengths. Therefore, the area of this square is equal to

Content:
[MATH: 1\,\textrm{m}\times 1\,\textrm{m} = 1\,\textrm{m}^2.]
The unit of area [MATH: (\textrm m^2)] we used is called a square meter. In this case, we say that the area of our square is one square meter.

Content:
In previous lessons, we learned that length can also be measured in kilometers [MATH: (\textrm{km}),] centimeters [MATH: (\textrm{cm}),] and millimeters [MATH: (\textrm{mm}).] Each of these length units has a corresponding area unit:

Content:
- A square with sides of length [MATH: 1\,\textrm{km}] has an area of [MATH: 1\,\textrm{km}^2,] or one square kilometer.
- A square with sides of length [MATH: 1\,\textrm{cm}] has an area of [MATH: 1\,\textrm{cm}^2,] or one square centimeter.
- A square with sides of length [MATH: 1\,\textrm{mm}] has an area of [MATH: 1\,\textrm{mm}^2,] or one square millimeter.

Content:
The same idea applies when measuring area in customary units. For example:

Content:
- A square with sides of length [MATH: 1\,\textrm{in}] has an area of [MATH: 1\,\textrm{in}^2,] or one square inch.
- A square with sides of length [MATH: 1\,\textrm{ft}] has an area of [MATH: 1\,\textrm{ft}^2,] or one square foot.
